posts.title: High-throughput persistence, part 1: one Lambda is not a queue
posts.summary: One Lambda writing straight to DynamoDB could not hold the burst: the payload was rejected, then the connections reset. Splitting the function and putting a queue between the reader and the writer is what made the next measurement possible.
posts.imageAlt: A dense crowd, used as a stand-in for a burst of requests

posts.title: High-throughput persistence, part 2: delay the rush
posts.summary: A five-second delivery delay kept the writers from waking up in the same instant. That gap was enough to persist roughly 800,000 records, and then a larger run, with no errors in the measurement.
posts.imageAlt: Balls waiting in a line, a stand-in for a queue
